items.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998
items.q: I says to Finegan, “How come you picked me to play oboe in the band?”

ctx.x: What did the audition consist of? Just playing some of their charts?

Just sitting in and playing the charts. And one number they played was “Moonlight on the Ganges,” and I missed every note. I was so nervous, it was so difficult. And then six months later, after I been on the band, I never figured out how I got on the band, I says to Finegan, “How come you picked me to play oboe in the band?” I says, “I missed every note on ‘Ganges.’” He said, “You played two good bars on ‘When Hearts Are Young.’” And he says, “And the guys in the band wanted you.” So, which was another thing —…
It’s nice to have that support, yeah. Was there any talk about, was this a good idea to be trying to be forming a big band now, was it what, ‘52?
